correctness.rationale: Every length-two commutative chain ring admits Smith normal form diag(I_a, pi I_b, 0_c). The number of first matrices is G_q(n,a) q^(2na-a^2) G_q(n-a,b), and each kernel has q^(b+2c) elements; choosing n columns gives formula (1). Substituting finite-field rank products gives exact quadratic weight q^(5n²/2-(h²+b²)/2) Phi_n²/(Phi_a Phi_b Phi_c²). Uniform Phi_infinity^-4 domination by a summable discrete Gaussian gives l1 convergence, and Euler q-binomial/Jacobi identities evaluate the two parity-restricted limits as P_+³/2 +/- P_-³/2. The finite verifier independently enumerates all first matrices in small rings of split and mixed characteristic and all pairs in two F2-residue cases. Finite checks do not prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: Ordered zero-product probability is a canonical multiplicative invariant of finite matrix rings. Conditioning exposes a natural two-term-complex Smith defect rather than arbitrary parameter slices. The theorem determines the exact count for every matrix size, sharp fixed-q decay q^(-3n²/2), two distinct even/odd Euler-product-cube constants, and a nondegenerate tight limiting torsion law valid in split and mixed-characteristic chain rings. Each feature distinguishes a genuine structural probabilistic phenomenon, not a small-case recomputation.
